entities.name: Hasdai ibn Shaprut
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Hasdai ibn Shaprut (c. 915 – 975 CE), known also by his Arabic name Abu Yusuf ben Yitzhak ben Ezra, was a pivotal Jewish scholar, physician, diplomat, and patron of science and culture during the Golden Age of al-Andalus. Operating from the opulent court of the Umayyad Caliphate in Córdoba, his influence transcended religious and political boundaries, making him an indispensable figure in the caliphates of Abd al-Rahman III and his successor, al-Hakam II. His multi-faceted career positioned him at the nexus of Islamic, Jewish, and Christian worlds, profoundly shaping the intellectual and diplomatic landscape of 10th-century Iberia and beyond.

Ibn Shaprut's achievements were manifold and concrete. As the personal physician to Caliph Abd al-Rahman III, he gained unparalleled access and trust, which he leveraged for diplomatic and scholarly pursuits. He successfully negotiated peace treaties with the Christian kingdoms of León and Navarre, notably facilitating the marriage of Princess Urraca of Navarre to Ordoño III of León in 951 CE. His most celebrated scholarly contribution was organizing the translation of Dioscorides' monumental Greek medical text, *De Materia Medica*, into Arabic, a project that required Byzantine scholars and dramatically enriched Western pharmacological knowledge. Furthermore, he actively corresponded with Jewish communities across the diaspora, most famously with the Khazar Khaganate, seeking to understand their origins and affirm the existence of an independent Jewish polity.
